title: Make the four-registration trap loud

input.requestedOutcome: A new persisted field needs the persist helper, both client load paths, field_mapping.json and operation_schemas_model.json, plus a real column; miss any one and the data silently disappears. Build a drift check that fails CI when a model field has no mapping entry or a mapping entry has no column - restoring the capability of the deleted check_mapping_drift.js - plus an npm script scaffolding all registrations, and commit the ops.pierNote worked example into the repo. Source: allotment_v2/docs/workflows/07-data-persistence-api.md sections 4 and 10.5 (invariant 5).
acceptanceCriteria: A CI-runnable drift check compares os-backend/src/mapping/field_mapping.json against os-backend/src/mapping/operation_schemas_model.json and fails when a model column has no mapping entry or a mapping entry has no matching column
The check restores the capability of the deleted os-backend/scripts/check_mapping_drift.js (removed at 094dde1) without requiring the live blob or os_repo.js the old script needed
An npm script scaffolds (prints) all four registrations for a given field so a developer has a checklist plus copy-paste snippets
The ops.pierNote worked example (already-live, two-table json_text field) is committed as documentation, not as a new persisted field
Both mapping JSON files are read-only inputs to the check; the check and this task's own edits must never modify them
A GitHub Actions workflow wires the check into PRs, alongside (not replacing or modifying) the existing ci-boot-smoke.yml (LAM-16)
constraints: os-backend/src/mapping/field_mapping.json and operation_schemas_model.json are live persistence mappings - read and compare only, never modify
Do not edit allotment_v2/allotment_v2.html, server.js, or any SQL
Do not touch .github/workflows/ci-boot-smoke.yml (LAM-16, already on base) - add a sibling workflow file instead
Report the real drift count found against the current repo; do not tune the check to force a particular answer
Stage only the owned paths, explicitly, never git add -A / git add .
Exclusive owner of root package.json and .github/workflows/mapping-drift.yml this run
assumptions: docs/workflows/07 in the Jira text refers to allotment_v2/docs/workflows/07-data-persistence-api.md (verified: no docs/workflows/07* exists at repo root)
10.5 in the Jira text refers to item 5 in section 10's numbered invariant list (there is no literal heading numbered 10.5); that item is the exact four-registrations statement
The worktree was clean at start on agent/LAM-28-mapping-drift-check tracking origin/refactor/booking-v2-migration at HEAD e7d28f0

output.summary: Added tools/check-mapping-drift.mjs, a static CLI that diffs os-backend/src/mapping/field_mapping.json against operation_schemas_model.json table-by-table and fails (exit 1) when a model column has no mapping entry or a mapping entry has no column, restoring the capability (not the implementation) of the deleted os-backend/scripts/check_mapping_drift.js. Wired it into a new npm script (check:mapping-drift) and a new sibling CI workflow (.github/workflows/mapping-drift.yml) that runs on PRs into refactor/booking-v2-migration and main. Added tools/scaffold-registration.mjs (npm run scaffold:registration), a print-only CLI that emits the full four-registration checklist with copy-paste field_mapping.json / operation_schemas_model.json / ALTER TABLE snippets for a given field and table set, making no file edits. Documented the trap, the check, and the scaffold tool in docs/development/four-registration-trap.md, including the already-live ops.pierNote worked example committed as documentation only. Ran the drift check against the real, current repo before writing anything else: it reports 0 drift (130 tables, all in lockstep), which is recorded honestly as the genuine finding rather than tuned toward any particular answer.

decisions: Compare field_mapping.json and operation_schemas_model.json directly against each other (table-by-table, field-name-by-column-name) rather than reimplementing the deleted script's live-blob decompose/assemble round-trip, which needs os_repo.js and a real sample blob; the two JSON files are self-contained, static, and are exactly the two of the four registrations that section 10 invariant 5 calls out as mechanically checkable

scaffold-registration.mjs never writes to field_mapping.json or operation_schemas_model.json - it only prints - because the task forbids editing those files and an auto-mutating script on a live persistence mapping is the class of over-eager automation CLAUDE.md section 4 warns against

Ran the drift check against the real, current repo before writing any other artifact, per the task's instruction not to tune the check until it reports zero; it reported 0 drift immediately, documented honestly as the genuine finding rather than adjusted or hidden
New CI workflow is a sibling file (mapping-drift.yml), not an edit to the existing ci-boot-smoke.yml, per the task's explicit instruction to leave that file alone
risks: The drift check cannot see the other three registrations (persist helper, both client load paths) - those are structural JavaScript inside allotment_v2.html, not tabular data; this is called out explicitly in the new doc so mapping-drift CI passing is not mistaken for all four registrations being correct

mapping-drift.yml's actual GitHub Actions execution was not verified end-to-end (no CI runner/network in this sandbox) - only its single npm run check:mapping-drift step was verified locally, and its YAML was checked by hand rather than with a linter
dependencies: Builds on (does not modify) .github/workflows/ci-boot-smoke.yml from LAM-16, already merged onto this base at e7d28f0
followUps: Consider whether branch protection on refactor/booking-v2-migration should mark the new mapping-drift check as required to merge - that is a repo-settings change outside this task's scope, same caveat as ci-boot-smoke.yml's own header comment

A future task could extend check-mapping-drift.mjs to also fail CI on db_type/column-type disagreement (currently 0 mismatches, verified, but nothing enforces that continuously since this task's scope was limited to entry-presence, not type-agreement)
rollback: Revert this task's commit on agent/LAM-28-mapping-drift-check, or drop the added files (tools/check-mapping-drift.mjs, tools/scaffold-registration.mjs, docs/development/four-registration-trap.md, .github/workflows/mapping-drift.yml) and the two new package.json script entries. No data, schema, or runtime app code is affected - rollback is purely removing tooling/docs/CI and is safe at any time.
